summary: Independent review of the test-only addition (real-FFmpeg reap-and-resume coverage), run with ffmpeg present so the reviewer could execute it. Verdict: worth having; it fails against a pristine pre-PR checkout. Findings addressed this round: (H1) the aggregate published-duration band was direction-blind - skipping content moves the total DOWN toward source duration and reads healthier than a correct resume, so the assertion was replaced with an ffprobe probe of where the resumed media actually begins, asserting it never lands past the coverage point and never more than a GOP behind. Verified: anchor 5.0s late now fails (resume begins 17.460s vs 15.000s coverage, 2.460s missing), 7.5s late fails, pre-PR index arithmetic fails. (M1) the duplicate/non-ascending segment-number assertions were unreachable - hlsenc under +append_list renumbers as start_number plus parsed entries, so resumeSegNum is not observable from output; removed and documented, that return pinned by unit tests instead. (M3) the race comment was false - the local locked wait removes the v.exited half but not Cmd.ProcessState written inside exec.Cmd.Wait, so the file does add reports 2->4; comment corrected, CI does not run -race. (M4/L2/L3) anchorHint now gated on failure direction and reads SegmentDuration from matrixConfig; the wait surfaces ffmpeg's error and stderr so a launch failure is not misreported as a skip. PUSHED BACK with evidence on H1's central example: the reviewer claimed an anchor 2.5s late 'skips one whole segment'; measured, it lands at 14.952s against a 15.000s boundary - a 48ms join, not a skip. -noaccurate_seek quantises to the key-frame grid so sub-GOP anchor error is absorbed; the lower total was a better join, not lost content. Deterministic across 6 runs. Adds 13s to the package. Scope: one new test file, no production change.
